title: "TreeCluster genotype constellations"

date: "2025-10-17"

## Descrip
Make genotype constellations across 8 segments using the output of TreeCluster max pairwise patristic distance clustering (cutoff 0.03, 0.02, ... )
Segment order as applied by Youk et al 2023: "genotype is determined by the gene constellation enerated by concatenating the clusters of each virus strain by following gene segment order; PB2|PB1|PA|HA|NP|NA|M|NS"
Singletons will not be treated as distinguishable with blanks (clades labelled for ex, PB1-single1_..., will be PB1-_...)

# Setup
## libs
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gtools)
library(NatParksPalettes)
library(ggalluvial)
library(cowplot)
library(ggh4x)
```

## ins and outs
```{r}
## Choice threhold
thresh<-"0.04"

#input
files.in<-list.files("../01_tc_evaluate/2026-02-09_treecluster_maxclade_eval_out/",
                     pattern=paste0(thresh,".csv"), full.names = T) %>% 
  str_subset(pattern="tc-out") %>% mixedsort()

##also need meta input to lookup sample for sequence names/nuc names
#use the filtered metadata after removing temp outliers
meta.fold<-"../../../01_fasttree/ft_rooted_outliers/2026-01-14_rem-outliers/rem_out/"
meta.in<-list.files(meta.fold, pattern="resid.csv",full.names = T) %>% 
  mixedsort()
l.seg<-length(meta.in)

#output fold
f.out<-paste0(Sys.Date(),"_", thresh,"_tc_genotypes_out/")
if(!dir.exists(f.out)){dir.create(f.out)}

#plotting theme
plot.theme<-theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  panel.background = element_rect("grey95"), 
                  axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
                  text=element_text(size=10,face="bold"),
                  legend.text=element_text(size=8),
                  axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 45,hjust=1,vjust=1))
plot.theme.x<-plot.theme+
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 45,hjust=1,vjust=1))

#plot segment colors
segments<-c("PB2","PB1","PA","HA","NP","NA","M","NS") #order for genotypes
segments.ms<-segments %>% mixedsort
segment.cols<-natparks.pals(name="Yellowstone", n=length(segments))
segment.cols<-segment.cols[c(1,5,2,4,6,3,8,7)]
names(segment.cols)<-segments
```

## Join the metadata and treecluster assignments to concat a genotype of clusters by sample
```{r}
meta.og<-meta<-tc<-replicate(n=l.seg, vector())
for(i in 1:l.seg){
  tc[[i]]<-read.csv(files.in[i])
  meta[[i]]<-read.csv(meta.in[i])
  #check same seg/order, all names present
  tc[[i]]$seg[1]==meta[[i]]$segment[1]
  all(tc[[i]]$SequenceName %in% meta[[i]]$seq_new)
  #take meta columns we need only. genotype is from genoflu
  meta[[i]]<- meta[[i]] %>% select(seq_new, sample, segment)
  colnames(meta[[i]])[1]<-c("SequenceName")
  #take tc columns needed
  tc[[i]]<-tc[[i]] %>% select(SequenceName, cluster, seg)
  #make singletons generic name - don't treat singleton clusters as unique!
  tc[[i]]$cluster [str_which(tc[[i]]$cluster,"s_")]<-"s"
  #Make a concatenated name
  tc[[i]]<-tc[[i]] %>% unite("segcluster", seg,cluster, sep="-", remove = T)
  # table(tc[[i]]$segcluster)
  #join meta onto the tc output
  meta[[i]]<-left_join(meta[[i]], tc[[i]], by="SequenceName")
  colnames(meta[[i]])[str_which(colnames(meta[[i]]),"segcluster")]<-
    paste0(meta[[i]]$segment[1], "_segcluster")
  meta.og[[i]]<-meta[[i]]
  meta[[i]]<-meta[[i]] %>% select(-segment, -SequenceName)
}

# Function to join all dataframes by "sample"
meta.all <- reduce(meta, full_join, by = "sample")

#lookin goood, now concatenate the clsuter cols
clustcols<-paste(segments, "segcluster",sep="_")
meta.all<-meta.all %>% unite("new_geno", all_of(clustcols), sep="_", remove = F)

length(unique(meta.all$new_geno)) #5042
length(unique(meta.all$HA)) #581

#1988 unique genotypes for 0.1 #2011 if singletons are treated as diff with 0.1. 
#7676 unique genotypes for 0.02 
# 5400 unique genotypes for 0.03 
# 3509 unique genotypes for 0.05 #3603 with singleton diff 0.05

#Join genotypes back on to individual metafiles by isolate name (to connect directly the seqname to the genotype and clade for fuuture plots)
for(i in 1:l.seg){
  meta.og[[i]]<-left_join(meta.og[[i]], meta.all[,c("sample","new_geno")], by="sample")
  write.csv(meta.og[[i]], paste0(f.out, segments.ms[i], "_meta_newgeno.csv"))
}
```

## Look at distrib of new_geno size and composition
## Plot clusters and new_geno frequencies
```{r}
## Make a long version 
meta.all.long<-meta.all %>% pivot_longer(cols=3:ncol(meta.all) ,names_to = "segment", values_to="cluster")
meta.all.long$segment<-str_replace_all(meta.all.long$segment, "_segcluster","")
meta.all.long$segment<-factor(meta.all.long$segment, levels=segments)
# which(is.na(meta.all.long$segment))

#filter out minor new_genos for now
meta.all.count<-meta.all %>% group_by(new_geno) %>% count() %>% arrange(-n)
#minors have less than 50 detections
Minors<-meta.all.count$new_geno [meta.all.count$n<50] %>% unique
Majors<-meta.all.count$new_geno [meta.all.count$n>=50] %>% unique

length(Minors); length(Majors)
nrow(meta.all.count) #70 diff
 
#HOw many major (non minor) genotypes??
meta.all.count %>%
  filter(!new_geno %in% Minors) %>% nrow() #83 for 0.03
##plot new_genos overall counts. not ordered
geno.ord<-meta.all.count$new_geno[order(meta.all.count$n, decreasing = T)]
meta.all.long$new_geno<-factor(meta.all.long$new_geno, levels=geno.ord)

```

## Analyze by common sample (wide)
```{r}
#make this a count of each genotype and the composite clusters
colnames(meta.all)<-str_replace_all(colnames(meta.all), "_segcluster","")
colnames(meta.all)

colnames(meta.all)[which(colnames(meta.all)=="NA")]<-"xNA" #prevents issue with NA
segments.x<-str_replace_all(segments, "NA","xNA")
meta.all_f<-meta.all %>%
  dplyr::group_by(new_geno, PB2, PB1, PA, HA, NP, xNA, M ,NS) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(.groups="rowwise",
            Freq=n())
  
#Filter out with Freq<10 in plots
#although note that many have full caldes, but no genotype assignment
nrow(meta.all_f) #3509 unique genotypes

## How many are singletons??
length(which(meta.all_f$Freq==1)) #2804 0.04
nrow(meta.all_f) - length(which(meta.all_f$Freq==1)) #2238 at 0.04
# 3109/5400*100 #57.6% singletons
2238/nrow(meta.all_f) #44.4%
## How many major with >=50
meta.all_f %>% filter(!new_geno %in% Minors) %>% nrow #122 at 0.04

## how many genotypes have NA for 2+ segmnets??
cols_to_check <- segments %>% str_replace_all("NA","xNA")
# Identify rows with N or more NAs among selected columns
rows_with_N_or_more_NAs <- meta.all %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(num_NA = sum(is.na(c_across(all_of(cols_to_check))))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(num_NA >= 2)
rows_with_N_or_more_NAs %>% nrow() #47 for N=2
length(unique(rows_with_N_or_more_NAs$new_geno)) #47
```


## Alluvial plot of clusters connected by genotypes
```{r}
# use an alluvial plot to connect clusters to common category
#count for ordering
meta.all_f$new_geno<-factor(meta.all_f$new_geno, levels=geno.ord)

#only major genos
meta.all_f %>%
  filter(Freq >= 50) %>%
  ggplot(aes(axis1=PB2, axis2=PB1, axis3=PA , axis4=HA, 
             axis5=NP,axis6=xNA, axis7=M , axis8=NS, 
             y=Freq)) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = segments, expand = c(.05, .01)) +
  xlab("Segment clusters by treecluster genotype [N>=50]") +
  ylab("N sequence")+
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = new_geno),width=0.6,decreasing = F) +
  geom_stratum(width=0.6,decreasing = F) +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)),decreasing = F,size=3) +
  plot.theme+
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x=element_text(size=rel(1.4)))+
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option="D")
  # guides(fill=guide_legend(nrow=2, title="Genotype"))

ggsave(paste0(f.out, "alluvial_clusters_genotype50.tiff"),width=10, height=6, units="in")
```

## comparison with the genoflu clusters and genotypes
```{r}
meta2<-replicate(n=l.seg, vector())
for(i in 1:l.seg){
  meta2[[i]]<-read.csv(meta.in[i])
  meta2[[i]]<- meta2[[i]] %>% select(sample, genotype)
}
#Join them all together and extract uniques
meta2.all<-bind_rows(meta2)
meta2.all<-meta2.all[-which(duplicated(meta2.all$sample)), ]
nrow(meta2.all) #29,748 isolate names 

#Join the new genotypes by isolate name
meta2.all<-left_join(meta2.all, meta.all[,c("sample","new_geno")], by="sample")

#co-occurence of genotypes
t<-table(meta2.all$genotype, meta2.all$new_geno) %>% as.data.frame()
t<-t[t$Freq>0,]
t<-t[order(t$Freq,decreasing = T),]
# head(t)
colnames(t)<-c("genoflu_genotype","new_genotype","Count")

## Evaluate co-occurence of genos for the most common ones

# # for 0.05, (text comments)
# t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="B3.13"),]
# ## All B3.13 genotypes are PB2-386_PB1-319_PA-363_HA-128_NP-207_NA-301_M-293_NS-338 (n=1579) (cutoff=0.05)
# t[which(t$new_genotype=="PB2-386_PB1-319_PA-363_HA-128_NP-207_NA-301_M-293_NS-338"),] #for 0.05
# #by my genos: also includes 24 with no genotypes assigned, 10 "notassigned", and 4 are B3.9
# t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="B3.2"),] #38 new genotypes, with varying M and PA clusters
# t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="B4.1"),] #16 new genotypes, with varying PA clusters
# t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="A3"),] #10 new genotypes, differ by NS clusters
# t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="B3.6"),] #all B3.6 are PB2-226_PB1-319_PA-363_HA-128_NP-207_NA-301_M-293_NS-338
# t[which(t$new_genotype=="PB2-226_PB1-319_PA-363_HA-128_NP-207_NA-301_M-293_NS-338"),]
# #by my genos: also includes B3.12, B3.8, B3.11, Minor79

#Results as above, but for 0.03
t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="B3.13"),]
## All but one B3.13 genotypes are "PB2-582_PB1-577_PA-737_HA-558_NP-354_NA-515_M-577_NS-837" (n=1578) (cutoff=0.03). One has different NS
t[which(t$new_genotype=="PB2-582_PB1-577_PA-737_HA-558_NP-354_NA-515_M-577_NS-837"),]
# our geno also has 24 blank and 10 NotAssigned

t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="B3.2"),] #183 new genotypes, with varying PA, HA, NA, M, NS
t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="B4.1"),] #21 new genotypes, with varying PA and M clusters
t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="A3"),] #14 new genotypes, differ by NS and PB2 clusters
t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="B3.6"),] #6 new genos, differing by NS. Mostly this one: 
t[which(t$new_genotype=="PB2-293_PB1-577_PA-737_HA-558_NP-426_NA-515_M-577_NS-837"),]
#by my genos: also includes 1 with blank genoflu genotype
t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="D1.1"),] #all PB2-600_PB1-342_PA-409_HA-257_NP-428_NA-137_M-485_NS-368
t[which(t$new_genotype=="PB2-600_PB1-342_PA-409_HA-257_NP-428_NA-137_M-485_NS-368"),]
#no other genos. Perfect match.
t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="A1"),] #50 new genotypes: # differ by PA, HA, NA, M

# for 0.02,
t[which(t$genoflu_genotype=="B3.13"),] #there are 15 diff new genotypes here for lower threshold, differing mostly based on PA


write.csv(meta2.all, paste0(f.out, "isolate_genos_compare.csv"))
write.csv(t, paste0(f.out, "genos_cooccurence.csv"),row.names = F)
```
